operator_io_quirks: Tiny DB: Manufacturers=6 rows, Products=11 rows; original_values lists are short (<=11), so rng.choices(k=min(5,len)) often returns near-duplicates.
Mixed-case table names (Manufacturers, Products) and mixed-case columns (Code, Name, Headquarter, Founder, Revenue, Price, Manufacturer); must be double-quoted in generated SQL.
No spaces in identifiers here, but BIRD-style quoting must still be applied uniformly.

Products.Price declared DECIMAL but storage class is integer (values 5,120,150,180,240); declared-type dispatch -> Number with scale from '(a[,b])' args absent -> default scale, is_int False (no 'int' in 'decimal').
Manufacturers.Revenue declared REAL, storage real, values are round floats (50.0..200.0).
Manufacturers.Code and Products.Code are INTEGER PKs, notnull=0 in pragma (SQLite PKs are implicitly NOT NULL but pragma reports 0).
FK Products.Manufacturer -> Manufacturers.Code, parent exists, parent is unique PK; no dangling FK, no self-FK, no composite PK.
Products.Name has distinct=10 < rows=11 (one duplicate name) but Name is NOT declared unique; no unique index besides PKs.
No CHECK constraints, no UNIQUE constraints, no views/triggers reported; DDL has trailing spaces and multi-line formatting.
All columns have null_rate 0.0 in the original; NOT NULL declared on Name/Headquarter/Founder/Price/Manufacturer but not on Code/Revenue.
VARCHAR(255) dispatches to String with length=255 (args[0]) -> very long random strings possible; DECIMAL with no args -> Number default scale.
Original is tiny so read_schema max_rows_per_table sampling is irrelevant; full read is fine.
operator_ts_expectations: Manufacturers.Code / Products.Code: Number fuzzer, int-like, PK single-column -> max_l0=inf, so fresh draws never reused; values perturbed by +-1/+-2 around uniform range [-10^scale,10^scale].

Manufacturers.Name/Headquarter/Founder, Products.Name: String fuzzer with length range up to 255; fresh random strings over 'a-zA-Z 0-9()' plus 50% contaminate (prefix/suffix/drop char) -> implausible names, likely FN on name-equality predicates.

Products.Price: Number fuzzer (DECIMAL, is_int False) -> float draws in [-10^scale,10^scale] with +-0.01/+-0.02 perturbation; original ints 5..240 not respected -> implausible prices, FN on price ranges.
Manufacturers.Revenue: Number fuzzer float; original 50..200 not respected -> wide range, FN on revenue thresholds.
Products.Manufacturer: FK child, draws from Manufacturers.Code final values with replacement -> duplicates and ties likely; good for join coverage but may create many-to-one skew.
PK filtering (sample_fresh_primary_keys) drops duplicate Code rows; with tiny tables and Number PK this rarely triggers, so PKs stay distinct.
No unique columns besides PK -> drop_unique_duplicates is a no-op here.
String fuzzer's int-like +1/-1 rule does not apply (names are not int-like); no date/time/bool columns so those fuzzers unused.
Table sizes: choose_table_sizes gives either ~30..230 per table or level-based (level0=1+30u, level1 x4 capped 2500) -> instances much larger than original 6/11 rows.
Likely FP source: missing ties/duplicates in original (e.g. Products.Name duplicate) not reproduced; DISTINCT/COUNT queries may differ.
Likely FN source: implausible string values and out-of-range numbers break equality/range predicates that gold SQL uses on the original.
